title: While renaming a file/folder with a long name, clamp wheel scrolls to whole lines; don't let half-lines appear
line: When renaming a file with a long name on the desktop, the mouse wheel now scrolls the name by whole lines and no line is shown cut in half.
explanation: The desktop's rename field limited its height to a multiple of the label icon size, which is not the real text line height, so it showed about 3.5 lines and always had a half-cut line. The mouse wheel was handled by the ScrollView's generic wheel handler, which scrolls a fixed 20 px per wheel line (about 3.4 text lines per notch), so the view drifted across line boundaries and could skip a line entirely (the reporter could not reach "5strawberry"). The field now uses the real line height for its maximum size, and a wheel-only MouseArea above the text scrolls it by whole lines (wheelScrollLines per notch, high-resolution wheels accumulated) and keeps it aligned to lines.

commits.message:
containments/desktop: scroll the rename field by whole lines

The rename field was not a whole number of lines tall and the wheel
moved it by a fixed amount of pixels, so half lines showed and lines
could be skipped. Size it to whole lines and scroll by whole lines too.

BUG: 523491

media.caption: Pure master: rename field after F2, then scrolled to the top and down one wheel notch at a time. Every stop shows a half-cut line and "11apple" is skipped.
With the fix, same steps: the field shows exactly 3 lines and each notch moves exactly 3 whole lines; every line is reachable.

reviews.text: Sizing maxHeight from the actual lineHeight instead of iconSizes.sizeForLabels cleanly eliminates the ~3.5-line clipping so whole lines fit in the rename editor. However, the wheel-intercepting MouseArea unconditionally swallows all wheel events—regressing smooth pixel-by-pixel touchpad scrolling (which the reporter noted already worked well) and horizontal scroll events—and fails to cap the per-notch step to the visible line count, so lines are still skipped whenever wheelScrollLines exceeds Plasmoid.configuration.textLines + 1.
changes: Ignore smooth pixel-based touchpad events and horizontal-only wheel events (e.g. set wheel.accepted = false and return when wheel.pixelDelta.y !== 0 || wheel.angleDelta.y === 0) so touchpads retain pixel-by-pixel scrolling.

Clamp the lines-per-notch scroll step to at most the visible line count (Plasmoid.configuration.textLines + 1) so users with textLines set to 1 or higher wheelScrollLines settings cannot skip lines completely.
Guard against editor.lineHeight <= 0 before dividing flickable.contentY / editor.lineHeight to prevent NaN contentY, and reset editor.wheelLines to 0 in onTargetItemChanged.

reviews.text: Fixes both causes Nate identified in c4: the field's max height used iconSizes.sizeForLabels instead of the real line height (so it was ~3.5 lines tall), and the generic ScrollView wheel step was a pixel amount unrelated to lines. With the field sized to whole lines and a wheel-only MouseArea (Qt.NoButton, only while the vertical scrollbar is on) stepping wheelScrollLines whole lines, the bottom clamp also lands on a line boundary. The before/after strips clearly show half-cut lines and the skipped line on master and clean 3-line steps reaching every line with the fix. Nits: touchpads now also step by lines although the reporter liked pixel scrolling there (keeping pixelDelta scrolling would be an option), and dragging the scrollbar can still stop mid-line. Neither matters for the wheel case the bug is about.
